title: SCM API: version negotiation (headers/payload) + client compatibility tests
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Background / why
Console and Optimize will call the Cost Model API (estimate + explain) and need deterministic semantics across deployments. We also need a forward-compatible story so we can add new cost components / signals without breaking existing clients.

This ticket implements SCM schema/API version negotiation and adds compatibility tests to ensure:
- older clients (no explicit versioning) continue to work
- newer clients can request a specific SCM version and get deterministic results
- clients get a clear, machine-readable error when they request an unsupported version, and can safely fall back

Scope
1) Implement version negotiation in Cost Model API (request parsing + validation)
2) Implement response fields for “requested version” vs “resolved version”
3) Implement unsupported-version error contract
4) Add compatibility + regression tests (unit + integration-style) covering:
   - no version specified (legacy behavior)
   - header-based request
   - payload-based request
   - conflict rules (header vs payload)
   - fallback behavior used by Console/Optimize clients

Proposed versioning contract (SCM v1)
Endpoints remain stable (no version in path):
- POST /cost-model/estimate
- POST /cost-model/explain

Client may specify a desired SCM version using either:
A) Header (preferred):
- X-Redwood-SCM-Version: "v1"

B) Payload (for non-HTTP callers / internal tooling):
- request.schema_version: "v1"

Precedence / conflict rules
- If both header + payload are provided and differ: reject with 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT and error_code=VERSION_CONFLICT.
- If only one is provided: use it.
- If none is provided: default to "v1" (current stable) for backwards compatibility.

Server response must include:
- scm_version_requested: string ("v1" or empty if not provided)
- scm_version_resolved: string (the version actually used; for this phase should always be "v1" unless/when we add v2)

Unsupported version behavior
If client requests a version that the server does not support:
- HTTP 406 NOT_ACCEPTABLE
- error_code: UNSUPPORTED_SCM_VERSION
- message: includes requested version
- details: include supported_versions (comma-separated string for now; keep flat in JSON response)

Notes / implementation details
- Ensure the resolved version is part of any internal memoization/cache key so results don’t leak across versions.
- Ensure audit logs / request logs include requested + resolved version (no customer payload logging).
- Add a metric counter for requested/resolved versions so we can see adoption and detect unexpected clients.

Acceptance criteria
- Cost Model service accepts version via header and/or payload and follows precedence rules above.
- When version omitted, behavior is identical to current v1 behavior (golden test vectors).
- Unsupported version returns 406 + correct error_code and includes supported versions.
- Compatibility tests cover: legacy (no version), explicit v1, explicit unsupported v2, and header/payload conflict.
- Console + Optimize client libraries can implement safe fallback: if UNSUPPORTED_SCM_VERSION, retry with v1 (bounded retry; no retry storms).

Testing plan
- Unit tests: request parsing/validation; error mapping; precedence logic.
- Golden tests: fixed input -> exact output snapshots for v1 (including scm_version_resolved field).
- Integration tests (staging):
  - Console-like caller: omit version; ensure success
  - Optimize-like caller: request "v2" then fallback to "v1"; ensure success and proper attribution fields present

Rollout
- Behind feature flag: scm_version_negotiation_enabled
- Enable in staging first, then prod canary tenants.
- Watch metrics:
  - unsupported_version rate
  - version_conflict rate
  - request success rate + latency deltas

Out of scope
- Defining SCM v2 schema changes (tracked separately)
- Customer-facing documentation changes (internal docs update can follow once merged)

comments: 2025-02-10 (Jordan Lee): Drafted negotiation contract. Strong preference for header-based selection to avoid path versioning; payload option kept for internal tooling and potential non-HTTP callers. Need explicit conflict rule to avoid ambiguous debugging.
2025-02-12 (Chloe Martin): Console backend can set header easily. Request: please include scm_version_resolved in response so UI/tooling can surface “SCM v1” in debug panels and support exports.

2025-02-13 (Hassan Mirza): Optimize wants to experiment with “vNext” in staging. Confirmed fallback behavior should be: on UNSUPPORTED_SCM_VERSION only, retry once with v1; do not retry on 4xx validation errors.

2025-02-18 (Amara Diallo): Gateway note: avoid path-versioning due to route duplication + auth policy divergence. Header-based approach aligns with existing internal service conventions. Please ensure CORS exposes the header for internal web Console calls (if applicable).

2025-02-20 (Jordan Lee): Implemented 406 NOT_ACCEPTABLE for unsupported versions. Added supported_versions to error details as a comma-separated string to keep response shape stable; will revisit structured error details when we formalize shared error envelopes.

2025-02-24 (Sean Gallagher): SRE request: add metric tags for requested_version/resolved_version but keep cardinality bounded (expected small set: v1, v2). Also add counter for version_conflict rejections to catch buggy clients quickly.

2025-02-27 (Jordan Lee): Added golden test vectors for v1 to lock down deterministic outputs (including scm_version_resolved). Added tests for: missing version defaults to v1; header vs payload conflict -> 400 VERSION_CONFLICT; unsupported v2 -> 406 UNSUPPORTED_SCM_VERSION.
2025-03-03 (Ethan Park): Reviewed PR. Requested change: ensure resolved version participates in internal cache key; otherwise future v2 could serve cached v1 results. Approved after follow-up commit.
2025-03-05 (Jordan Lee): Merged and deployed to staging behind flag. Next: coordinate with Console/Optimize to start sending requested version header once their clients are ready (separate tickets).
